note: Image/model library for Know more. Prefer models/*.glb when present; else images/*.svg. Replace placeholders with high-res art or 3D as assets arrive.

sun.name: Sun
sun.subtitle: Our star
sun.summary: A G-type main-sequence star at the center of the Solar System. It holds 99.8% of the system’s mass and drives Earth’s climate and seasons.

moon.name: Moon
moon.subtitle: Earth’s companion
moon.summary: Earth’s only natural satellite. Its phases, tides, and occultations are among the most useful cues for night-sky planning.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.subtitle: Innermost planet
mercury.summary: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun. Extremes of day and night temperature make it a challenging telescopic target near twilight.

venus.name: Venus
venus.subtitle: The morning / evening star
venus.summary: Earth’s twin in size, wrapped in a thick CO₂ atmosphere. Often the brightest planet; best seen as a crescent in a small telescope.

earth.name: Earth
earth.subtitle: Our home world
earth.summary: The only known world with liquid oceans and life. From space it is a blue marble with swirling clouds and a thin, fragile atmosphere.

mars.name: Mars
mars.subtitle: The Red Planet
mars.summary: A cold desert world with polar caps, giant volcanoes, and seasonal dust storms. Opposition nights are prime time for surface detail.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.subtitle: King of the planets
jupiter.summary: A gas giant with banded clouds and the Great Red Spot. Even binoculars reveal the four Galilean moons changing place night to night.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.subtitle: The ringed world
saturn.summary: Famous for its icy ring system. A small telescope shows the rings and Titan; ring tilt changes over Saturn’s long year.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.subtitle: The ice giant
uranus.summary: A pale cyan ice giant tipped on its side. Soft and featureless in small scopes; best hunted with a chart or app.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.subtitle: The blue planet
neptune.summary: The farthest major planet, deep blue from methane in its atmosphere. Tiny and challenging — a rewarding find for careful observers.

sirius.name: Sirius
sirius.subtitle: Alpha Canis Majoris
sirius.summary: The brightest star in the night sky. A nearby binary with a white-dwarf companion (Sirius B).

vega.name: Vega
vega.subtitle: Alpha Lyrae
vega.summary: A brilliant summer landmark and one corner of the Summer Triangle. Once used as a zero-point for the magnitude scale.

betelgeuse.name: Betelgeuse
betelgeuse.subtitle: Alpha Orionis
betelgeuse.summary: A red supergiant marking Orion’s shoulder. Famous for variability and as a future supernova candidate.

rigel.name: Rigel
rigel.subtitle: Beta Orionis
rigel.summary: A luminous blue-white star at Orion’s foot — one of the sky’s brightest beacons despite its great distance.

andromeda.name: Andromeda
andromeda.subtitle: M31 · nearest major galaxy
andromeda.summary: The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest large spiral to the Milky Way and a naked-eye target under dark skies.

sombrero.name: Sombrero
sombrero.subtitle: M104
sombrero.summary: An edge-on spiral with a bright nucleus and a dark dust lane — the Sombrero Galaxy.

triangulum.name: Triangulum
triangulum.subtitle: M33
triangulum.summary: The Triangulum Galaxy is a face-on spiral in the Local Group, often spotted near Andromeda.

pinwheel.name: Pinwheel
pinwheel.subtitle: M101
pinwheel.summary: A grand-design face-on spiral in Ursa Major — a classic deep-sky photographic target.
